baseline_definition: A generative world model for simulating and optimizing mobile wireless networks via counterfactual reasoning.
generated_definition: A diffusion-based world model that generates high-fidelity synthetic network environments to simulate and optimize wireless communication systems dynamically, enabling adaptive and robust network planning through learned probabilistic scenario generation.

baseline_definition: An autonomous agent framework using LLMs for closed-loop wireless network management tasks like slicing.
generated_definition: An AI-driven Large Language Model agent that dynamically orchestrates and optimizes network slicing and resource allocation by interpreting real-time network data and service requirements through natural language inputs and predictive analytics.

baseline_definition: A wireless foundation model designed to compress and reconstruct heterogeneous CSI feedback across varying configurations.
generated_definition: A channel state information (CSI) feedback framework that leverages a foundation model with a Mixture of Experts (MoE) architecture to dynamically select specialized expert networks for efficient and context-aware channel compression, optimizing feedback overhead across diverse wireless environments.

baseline_definition: A semantic communication framework using diffusion models for noise-resilient semantic transmission and reconstruction.
generated_definition: DSemCom-Net leverages diffusion probabilistic models with U-Net architectures to iteratively reconstruct and refine semantic information from noisy wireless signals, enabling robust, context-aware semantic communication that dynamically adapts to channel uncertainties.

baseline_definition: An end-to-end channel prediction model utilizing the Mamba architecture for linear-complexity temporal modeling.
generated_definition: A selective state space modeling framework that leverages Mamba's adaptive filtering principles to enhance channel prediction accuracy in MIMO systems by dynamically selecting the most relevant channel states for reliable transmission.

baseline_definition: A pilot-free channel inference framework using Flow Matching to map multimodal sensing data to channel matrices.
generated_definition: A pilot-free wireless channel estimation approach that leverages flow matching generative ODE models to reconstruct channel state information by learning continuous transformations of received signal distributions without explicit training pilots.

baseline_definition: A direct communication paradigm where LLMs exchange KV-Cache states instead of tokenized text.
generated_definition: A communication framework that leverages inter-model semantic exchange by dynamically fusing LLM key-value caches to optimize the transmission and interpretation of contextual knowledge across distributed AI agents and wireless networks.

baseline_definition: A semantic communication scheme using Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Knowledge Graphs for error correction.
generated_definition: A communication framework that leverages knowledge graphs to perform semantic decoding and error correction by contextualizing received signals within structured domain knowledge, enabling more accurate interpretation and recovery of transmitted information despite noise and distortions.

baseline_definition: A neuromorphic framework using Spiking Neural Networks for power-efficient beamforming and channel estimation.
generated_definition: A novel beamforming and OFDM channel estimation framework that leverages spiking neural networks to process temporal spike patterns for ultra-low latency, energy-efficient, and adaptive wireless signal optimization.

baseline_definition: A hybrid MAC protocol framework combining token-based LLM adaptation with lightweight neural distillation.
generated_definition: DistilledMAC Signaling leverages knowledge distillation from large language models to optimize MAC protocol signaling by enabling lightweight, context-aware decision-making for efficient medium access and reduced overhead in wireless networks.

baseline_definition: A security framework using meta-learning and GFlowNets for rapid adaptation of secure beamforming in mobile scenarios.
generated_definition: A physical layer security approach that leverages meta-learning to adaptively optimize directional modulation patterns, using generative flow networks to efficiently explore secure transmission states for robust and dynamic wireless confidentiality.

baseline_definition: A robust beam tracking method using Liquid Neural Networks to handle noisy, continuous-time channel dynamics.
generated_definition: A dynamic beamforming and tracking system that leverages Liquid Neural Networks to continuously adapt to rapidly changing wireless channel conditions in real-time, enabling ultra-responsive and efficient directional signal optimization.

baseline_definition: An indoor localization model replacing MLPs with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks to capture non-linear RSS-distance mappings.
generated_definition: KanoFi Localization leverages Kolmogorov-Arnold Network's universal functional decomposition to model complex WiFi RSS fingerprinting patterns, enabling highly accurate and computationally efficient indoor positioning by capturing nonlinear signal variations across environments.

baseline_definition: A self-evolving generative agent framework that designs and refines task-oriented workflows for specialized wireless tasks.
generated_definition: An autonomous generative agent that continuously evolves and optimizes network automation protocols by learning from real-time network data and adapting communication strategies without human intervention.

baseline_definition: A federated parameter-efficient fine-tuning paradigm for adapting large models under distributed learning settings.
generated_definition: FDAL is a wireless communication framework that enables distributed devices to collaboratively train AI models using federated learning enhanced with parameter-efficient fine-tuning (adapter tuning), minimizing data exchange and communication overhead while preserving model personalization and privacy.

baseline_definition: An indoor localization framework using xLSTM for temporal modeling and multimodal fusion of UWB and IMU data.
generated_definition: A hybrid indoor localization system that leverages Extended LSTM (xLSTM) to intelligently fuse Ultra-Wideband (UWB) ranging data with Visual-Inertial Odometry (VIO), enhancing positioning accuracy and robustness in complex indoor environments.

baseline_definition: A Llama-based platform for 5G network-slice orchestration and cloud-native service deployment.
generated_definition: An AI-driven 5G core orchestration framework that leverages Llama-2 large language models integrated with GitOps principles to automate and optimize dynamic network slicing deployment and lifecycle management through intelligent, declarative configurations.

baseline_definition: A traffic prediction model utilizing Retentive Networks (RetNet) to optimize Elastic Optical Network (EON) resources.
generated_definition: Retentive TrafficNet leverages RetNet's memory-efficient sequence modeling to predict network traffic patterns with long-term temporal dependencies, enabling dynamic and precise resource allocation in wireless communication systems.

baseline_definition: A framework utilizing quantum machine learning models to process wireless signals for sensing applications in AIoT.
generated_definition: Quantum-AIoT Sensing leverages quantum machine learning algorithms to enhance wireless sensing in AIoT devices, enabling ultra-fast, high-precision environmental perception and adaptive decision-making in complex wireless environments.

baseline_definition: A physics-grounded generative AI framework for mitigating hallucination in wireless communication tasks.
generated_definition: A channel estimation framework that leverages physics-informed generative AI models to accurately predict and reconstruct wireless channel states by embedding physical propagation laws into the generative process, enhancing estimation robustness and reducing pilot overhead.
